original_question:
When partial off-axis variation of the group velocity and longitudinal self-steepening are both present in the same direction, namely for

 i(1 - epsilon^2 partial_z^2) partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon partial_z)(|v|^2 v) = 0,

do solutions still exhibit self-steepening, or does the off-axis regularization suppress or qualitatively change that shock-like steepening effect?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 8 in §4.3 (“Mixing Several Phenomena”): for the mixed scalar model (72), which combines partial off-axis variation of the group velocity in the z-direction with longitudinal self-steepening in the same z-direction, the paper asks whether the solutions exhibit self-steepening. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact equation (72), the fact that both effects act in the same distinguished direction z, and the paper’s intended yes/no issue: whether partial off-axis regularization prevents self-steepening from occurring. That is essentially the content of Open Problem 8. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates this specifically for the scalar NLS-type equation (72) in §4.3, not as a broader question about all mixed models or about the vectorial equation. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should state that v is a complex-valued unknown, ε>0 is the small parameter, z is the propagation direction, and Δ is the full spatial Laplacian in the variables x=(X⊥,z). These conventions come from Notation 1 and the general scalar model (3). ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The paper’s terminology should be made explicit: 1-ε²∂²z is the example of partial off-axis variation of the group velocity in the z-direction, while (1+iε∂z) is the longitudinal self-steepening operator in that same direction. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The draft does not define what “self-steepening” means in the paper’s nearby discussion: it refers to the possible formation of optical-shock-type, asymmetric pulse profiles, not merely to generic blow-up or any steep gradient. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

A paper-faithful stand-alone formulation should note the nearby analytic context that partial off-axis dependence already raises unresolved local/global well-posedness issues in §4.1.4; Open Problem 8 is posed on top of that background. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
refined_question:
For the scalar cubic NLS-type equation

i(1-ε²∂²_z)∂_t v + Δv + (1+iε∂_z)(|v|²v)=0,

with complex-valued unknown v=v(t,x), ε>0, z the propagation direction, Δ the full spatial Laplacian, and where 1-ε²∂²_z models partial off-axis variation of the group velocity while iε∂_z(|v|²v) models longitudinal self-steepening in the same z-direction, do solutions exhibit the self-steepening phenomenon in the paper’s sense (optical-shock-type/asymmetric pulse-profile formation), or does the partial off-axis variation prevent self-steepening from taking place? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because §4.3 introduces exactly this mixed equation (72) as an example where several effects are present simultaneously, then immediately states: “one may wonder whether the partial off-axis variation of the group velocity prevents the self-steepening from taking place,” and packages that as Open Problem 8. The nearby context needed to decode the question is supplied earlier: §1.1/Notation 1 defines z, X⊥, Δ⊥, the scalar model (3), partial off-axis dependence, and self-steepening; §4.1.5 explains that self-steepening is associated with optical shocks and asymmetric pulse profiles; and §4.1.4 shows that even partial off-axis dependence alone already leaves well-posedness open. The algebraic checklist items from your instructions (homogeneity degree, nilpotency, phrases like “for all sufficiently large m”) are not relevant to this PDE open problem. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
